features.headline: Who will win MVP? Cy Young? Picks, analysis for 2026 MLB awards week
features.desc: Baseball's best players and managers of 2026 collect their hardware this week — starting tonight with the year's top rookies.
body: The baseball offseason has felt pretty normal so far, at least if you can put the overhanging labor negotiations out of your mind.
Some of that normalcy comes from the gradual easing into the initial phases of the hot stove season — contract options, roster maneuvering, free agency filing — that point toward next season.
That's administrative stuff, though, and not as fun as the parade in Milwaukee, or this week, when MLB hands out its major awards in what more or less closes the books on the 2026 season.

This year's awards week is an expansion of the usual routine because we have a new honor being handed out by the Baseball Writers' Association of America: the Reliever of the Year Award, which recognizes the top bullpen maestro from each league. Here's how this week's schedule lays out:

Monday: Rookie of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Tuesday: Manager of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Wednesday: Cy Young and Reliever of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Thursday: MVP (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network)
MLB Network will also air the MLB awards given out during a live ceremony in Las Vegas at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday.

Honors given out then include the Hank Aaron Award, Comeback Player of the Year, Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman Relievers of the Year, Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and selections for the All-MLB first and second teams.
Finalists for the major awards have already been announced. So let's see how things look before the hardware is handed out. Who might win? Who should win?

features.headline: Joe Burrow reaching new heights as Bengals face big test
features.desc: Burrow led the Bengals to their fourth straight win, and AFC North rival Pittsburgh is on deck.
body: MADRID — Joe Burrow talked a big game all offseason.
He wasn't shy about the aspirations for himself or the Cincinnati Bengals, which included a potential run at a Super Bowl.

Through eight games this season, Burrow and the team are backing all of that up. On an enormous stage, playing an international game in one of the world's most iconic venues in a standalone broadcast window, Burrow and the Bengals dazzled.

He was nearly flawless in a 34-17 victory Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons in the historic Santiago Bernabeu, Cincinnati's fourth straight win. And with his performance, he is in the mix for an award that has eluded him — Most Valuable Player.

"He should have [already] won the MVP," Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase said. "I said this when we went to the Super Bowl [to cap the 2021 season] and he didn't get it that year. I mean, he's up for it every year."

But this year, Burrow is working on his strongest case to date. According to ESPN Research, Burrow is the fifth player in NFL history to have at least 23 passing touchdowns and a 70% completion percentage or higher.
In three of those instances, that quarterback won MVP (Tom Brady, 2007; Aaron Rodgers, 2011; Peyton Manning, 2013).

Burrow dominated Sunday. He was 24-of-29 passing for 271 yards and four total touchdowns (three passing, one rushing). He became the fifth player in league history to have at least four passing or rushing touchdowns in four straight games.
Three of those players are in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Brady is the other one.

features.headline: Inside Justin Jefferson's miraculous catch for Vikings versus Bills in 2022
features.desc: In 2022 against the Bills, Jefferson leaped up and came down with one of "the greatest catches of all time."
body: EAGAN, Minn. — The play is commemorated everywhere.

It's the central ink of a tattoo that covers Justin Jefferson's left thigh. It's depicted on a life-size Fathead wall sticker in coach Kevin O'Connell's basement, and in a photograph hanging on the wall of the Minnesota Vikings' practice facility.

There is a private-issue hoodie sweatshirt that cleverly incorporates Jefferson's uniform number with what he agrees is the catch of his life: A leaping, one-handed grab to convert fourth-and-18 during a wild overtime victory over the Buffalo Bills in 2022.

Several Vikings staff members will be wearing that sweatshirt Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC), where the Vikings and Bills will meet for the first time since Jefferson changed the course of his career.

Already a two-time Pro Bowl receiver by then at age 23, Jefferson went on to lead the NFL in catches and receiving yards while earning his first All-Pro honor and the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year award.

His statistics have slipped in the past two seasons as the Vikings have transitioned through four different starting quarterbacks, and players and coaches alike acknowledged his frustration during a 33-yard game last Sunday against the Detroit Lions.
But even if he never returns to his previous production, Jefferson can rest assured that he long ago cemented himself in NFL history.
"If you talk about the greatest catches of all time," said Vikings assistant receivers coach Derron Montgomery, "how can you leave out that one?"

features.headline: Premier League VAR review: Should Man United's equalizing goal have been allowed?
features.desc: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
body: The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.
Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship.

With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday.
Referee: Chris Kavanagh VAR: Craig Pawson Time: 96 minutes Incident: Possible foul in Manchester United's equalizing goal.
What happened: Bruno Fernandes swung in a last-chance corner kick as Man United threw every player they had on the pitch, including keeper Senne Lammens, into the penalty area at 4-3 down.
Patrick Dorgu outjumped the Aston Villa defenders and, with keeper Zion Suzuki flapping at the ball, nodded home what seemed like a straightforward header into the net.

However, Suzuki believed he was fouled by opposite number Lammens as the United No. 1 attempted to block the Villa keeper. Lammens made contact with Suzuki while neither looking at the ball nor making any attempt to play it.
Referee Kavanagh was unmoved by the appeals, yellow-carding Suzuki for his protests and awarding the goal.

features.headline: Which player has the most career points in NHL history?
features.desc: Wayne Gretzky leads the list of NHL players with the most career points. Check out other top performers now.
body: Wayne Gretzky owns a laundry list of NHL records, including the mark for the most career points.
A player earns a point by either scoring a goal or getting an assist, which is credited to up to two players who pass the puck toward a teammate who scores.
Gretzky's 894 career goals plus his 1,963 career assists give him a grand total of 2,857 points over his illustrious 20-year career. That's nearly 1,000 more than any other player.

features.headline: What Yankees, Mets can do this winter to meet their 2027 goals
features.desc: The 2026 MLB season didn't go as either New York team planned. Here's how they can flip the script next year.
body: With a lockout looming on Dec. 1, the consensus across Major League Baseball is that November will be a frenetic month, similar to the lead-up to the 2021 lockout. Free agents will come off the board. Trades will be made. There will be a flurry of player movement before the league shuts down.

The action, according to sources, is expected to start as soon as next week, when the industry convenes at the general managers meetings in Las Vegas. And you can expect the two New York clubs will be involved.

The Yankees and Mets experienced very different versions of disappointment in 2026. The Yankees reached the postseason for the eighth time in nine years under manager Aaron Boone, only to get bounced by an American League East rival in the division series for the second straight year.
The Mets, meanwhile, did not make the playoffs for the second consecutive season, finishing last in the National League East despite having one of baseball's two most expensive payrolls.

Both teams will dabble in the free agent and trade markets to bolster their rosters this offseason. Here are three needs we believe each team will address to get over the hump by the time Opening Day comes around — whenever that is.
1. Rebuild the bullpen (starting with closer David Bednar?)

Pitching was not the problem for the Yankees in 2026. They led the majors in staff ERA by a good margin. But while they have a surplus of starters, they'll need to fill out their bullpen again this offseason.
As it stands, left-hander Brent Headrick is the only reliever under team control for next season who had at least 17 appearances in 2026.
